rulings.Case Title: ELEN MEDER VS. CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH CARE SERVICES
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion; Motion To Stay Operation Of Administrative Decision Under Ccp 1094.5(G); Memornadum Of Points And Authorities
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, Line 2. Petitioner's motion to stay administrative decision is DENIED. Before the court is Petitioner's petition for a writ of administrative mandamus under Code of Civil Procedure section 1094.5. Section 1094.5(g) allows the court to "stay the operation of the administrative order or decision." The decision that forms the basis of this case was adopted on April 6, 2026. The administrative law judge ("ALJ") ruled that the termination of petitioner's benefits was improper because respondent failed to provide at least 30-days-notice to petitioner to respond to the verifications. The ALJ ordered Respondent to (1) rescind the 11/13/25 notice of action, (2) send petitioner a MC355 Request for Information requesting income verification/account information with at least 30-days-notice; and (3) redetermine petitioner's and her husband's eligibility. Respondent correctly notes that petitioner is not truly seeking to stay this decision. Rather, she seeks "a stay of the operation of the administrative decision discontinuing Medi-Cal benefits effective July 1, 2026." (Petitioner's Notice of Motion, 2:16-17.) A notice of action issued on 6/10/26-not the administrative decision that is the subject of this action-caused the termination of benefits on July 1, 2026. The court cannot stay that notice of action as petitioner is currently litigating the propriety of that action. (Meder Decl., par. 11, Ex. F.) Petitioner must exhaust her administrative remedy. Petitioner's other requests for affirmative relief are also improper under CCP 1094.5(g). (Blackburn v. Sarsfield (1981) 125 Cal.App.3d 143, 150 ["Once eligibility for social services has been established, moreover, an award of retroactive payments is appropriate even though the services for which payments are sought were never performed."].) Respondent is ordered to prepare a proposed order which repeats the above text verbatim and email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the time set for hearing. Good cause appearing, the court orders the 5/20/2021 default and 5/20/2021 judgment vacated. The matter is returned to the master calendar. rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, Line 8. DEFENDANT REVI TECHNOLOGIES, INC.'s MOTION FOR WITHDRAWAL OF ATTORNEY OF RECORD. Before the court is a Motion to be Relieved as Counsel from Counsel David N. Buffington and GLC Law Group, P.C., counsel of record for Defendant Revi Technologies Inc. The motion is GRANTED. Good cause appearing, the motion is granted. Prior to the time set for hearing, Moving Party must lodge by email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org an updated proposed order on MC-053 with accurate information inserted, where appropriate. Note the Order will not be effective until Counsel files a Proof of Service of the executed order. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(302/JMQ)
